315	
316	> **First — is this an agent at all?** If the task is deterministic logic with no LLM reasoning (validate data, call an API with custom auth, transform records, upload/download files), it's a **Python Coded Function** — not an agent. Use the [`uipath-functions`](/uipath:uipath-functions) skill instead of this one. 2	
3	Coded agents in flows use the `uipath.core.agent.{key}` node with `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`. Three patterns exist, distinguished by where the agent lives.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Pattern 1: In-Solution Coded Agent
8	
9	The coded agent lives as a sibling folder inside the same solution as the flow. The flow references it with `section: "In this solution"`; the runtime resolves the node via the Studio Web projects API.
10	
11	- **Agent-side scaffolding:** [embedding-in-flows.md](embedding-in-flows.md)
12	- **Wiring the agent's inputs:** [embedding-in-flows.md § Wiring the Agent's Inputs](embedding-in-flows.md#wiring-the-agents-inputs)
13	- **Flow node JSON shape + top-level `bindings[]` + `definitions[]` entry:** uipath-maestro-flow skill, agent-plugin reference (In-solution variant)
14	
15	The node-type's `{key}` is the local `resource.key` minted by `uip solution project add` (written to `resources/solution_folder/process/agent/<name>.json`) and surfaced by `uip maestro flow registry list --local`.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Pattern 2: Published Coded Agent
20	
21	The coded agent is deployed to Orchestrator as a standalone tenant resource. Any solution can reference it.
22	
23	**When to use:** reused across flows, independent versioning, already deployed.
24	
25	```bash
26	uip codedagent deploy --my-workspace
27	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
28	```
29	
30	**Capture the package key from the deploy command's own output** — `uip codedagent deploy` prints JSON containing the package `Key` (an Orchestrator-assigned GUID). That GUID is the `resourceKey` used in the flow node's `type` (`uipath.core.agent.<resourceKey>`) and `model.bindings.resourceKey`. Always run `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` after deploy to refresh the local flow registry cache, but do NOT depend on `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.agent"` to return the deployed agent — that search only enumerates built-in node types (`uipath.agent.autonomous`, etc.); user-deployed coded agents do not appear there, so an empty result is the *expected* state and is NOT a sign the deploy failed.
31	
32	Fallback discovery paths if the deploy output is unavailable or unparseable, **tried in order** — stop at the first one that returns the package:
33	
34	1. `uip or packages list --search "<agent-name>" --output json` (tenant feed listing). Returns 404 on tenants where the caller lacks `Orchestrator.Packages.View` scope — if so, move to (2).
35	2. `uip or processes list --folder-path "<FolderName>" --output json` if the agent was deployed via `--folder` rather than `--my-workspace`.
36	
37	If all paths return empty / 404, the deploy command's stdout JSON is authoritative — re-run the deploy and capture its output rather than chasing post-hoc discovery endpoints.
38	
39	For the flow node JSON shape, see the uipath-maestro-flow skill agent-plugin reference (Published variant). `model.section` is `"Published"`.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Pattern 3: Tool Resource for Another Agent
44	
45	The coded agent is a tool that another agent (inline or published) can call. Requires deploying the coded agent to Orchestrator first.
46	
47	**Resource file** at `<AgentProject>/resources/<ResourceName>/resource.json`:
48	
49	```json
50	{
51	  "$resourceType": "tool",
52	  "type": "agent",
53	  "name": "MyCodedAgent",
54	  "description": "What this agent does (shown to the parent LLM for tool selection)",
55	  "location": "external",
56	  "properties": {
57	    "processName": "<CODED_AGENT_PROCESS_NAME>",
58	    "folderPath": "<FOLDER_PATH>"
59	  },
60	  "inputSchema":  { "type": "object", "properties": { "userInput": { "type": "string" } } },
61	  "outputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "content":   { "type": "string" } } },
62	  "id": "<UUID>",
63	  "referenceKey": ""
64	}
65	```
66	
67	Coded agents use `location: "external"`.

62	## Generated Files
63	
64	| File | Purpose |
65	|---|---|
66	| `pyproject.toml` | Project metadata and dependencies |
67	| `main.py` | Agent entrypoint |
68	| `<framework>.json` | Framework config (LangGraph / LlamaIndex / OpenAI Agents) |
69	| `uipath.json` | Runtime options, pack options, `functions` map |
70	| `entry-points.json` | Input / output schemas from Pydantic models |
71	| `bindings.json` | Runtime bindings |
72	| `uv.lock` | Dependency lockfile |
73	| `.uipath/telemetry.json` | Telemetry configuration |
74	| `AGENTS.md`, `.agent/` | Documentation |

76	## `uipath.json`
77	
78	```json
79	{
80	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
81	  "runtimeOptions": {
82	    "isConversational": false
83	  },
84	  "packOptions": {
85	    "fileExtensionsIncluded": [],
86	    "filesIncluded": [],
87	    "filesExcluded": [],
88	    "directoriesExcluded": [],
89	    "includeUvLock": true
90	  },
91	  "functions": {}
92	}
93	```
94	
95	**Key fields:**
96	- **`runtimeOptions.isConversational`** - scaffold defaults to `false` (single-shot). Building a chat/conversational agent? Flip to `true` BEFORE `uip codedagent init` so `entry-points.json` gets the chat shape. See [conversational-agents](../capabilities/conversational-agents.md).
97	- **`packOptions`** - Control which files are included when packaging for deployment
98	- **`functions`** - Entrypoint mappings (format: `"file_path:function_name"`)

100	### `packOptions.directoriesExcluded` for solution context
101	
102	When the agent project is registered in a solution and uploaded via `uip solution upload`, the agent directory is bundled into the solution archive. Set `directoriesExcluded` to keep Python build artifacts out of the archive:
103	
104	```json
105	"packOptions": {
106	  "directoriesExcluded": [".venv", "__pycache__"],
107	  "includeUvLock": true
108	}
109	```
110	
111	`.venv/` is hundreds of MB of installed wheels and breaks uploads. `__pycache__/` is ephemeral bytecode. Both regenerate from `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` on the target side. Without these exclusions, `uip solution upload` produces an oversized archive that can be rejected by Studio Web.
112	
113	- `isConversational: true` for chat-style agents.
114	- `packOptions` controls `.nupkg` contents at deploy time.

7	## Sibling Folder Structure

9	The `<resourceKey>` is the local UUID minted by `uip solution project add` — stable the moment the agent joins the solution.
10	
11	```

14	├── resources/                      # created and maintained by `uip solution project add`
15	│   └── solution_folder/
16	│       ├── process/agent/<CodedAgentProject>.json   # holds the `resource.key` UUID
17	│       └── package/<CodedAgentProject>.json
18	├── <FlowProject>/
19	│   ├── <FlowName>.flow
20	│   └── project.uiproj
21	└── <CodedAgentProject>/
22	    ├── main.py                     # agent entrypoint
23	    ├── pyproject.toml              # Python project config
24	    ├── uipath.json                 # UiPath project config
25	    ├── entry-points.json           # generated by `uip codedagent init`
26	    ├── bindings.json               # runtime bindings
27	    ├── main.mermaid                # generated graph diagram
28	    ├── project.uiproj              # Studio Web project metadata
29	    ├── .env                        # environment variables

35	### Key differences from a published coded agent
36	
37	- **`resource.key`** is minted locally at `uip solution project add` time, not by Orchestrator at `uip codedagent deploy` time
38	- **No `codedagent deploy`** — the agent ships inside the solution package
39	- **Registry discovery is `--local`** (reads `resources/solution_folder/process/` files); no login or `registry pull` required

42	## Scaffolding the Sibling-Folder Coded Agent
43	
44	The full end-to-end workflow (solution init → flow scaffold → agent scaffold → register → wire → validate) is owned by [`quickstart.md` § Scenario 2](quickstart.md#quick-start-scenario-2--in-solution-coded-agent-in-a-flow). This file covers the agent-side detail of step 3 (scaffold) and step 5 (registration) in finer detail; the canonical sequence stays in the quickstart so it remains executable in one pass.
45	
46	If the solution and flow project don't yet exist, run `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` and then `uip maestro flow init "<FlowName>"` from inside the solution **before** the steps below — those calls are the start of Scenario 2.
47	
48	1. From the solution directory, create the agent folder and scaffold inside it:
49	
50	   ```bash

52	   cd <CodedAgentProject>
53	   uv venv --python 3.13
54	   source .venv/bin/activate       # .venv/Scripts/activate on Windows
55	   uv pip install <FRAMEWORK_PACKAGE>   # e.g. uipath for Coded Function

58	   uv sync

60	
61	   For a simple stub with no LLM call, use the Coded Function framework
62	   (`uipath` package). This avoids downloading the full LangGraph or
63	   LlamaIndex stack and keeps the setup fast.
64	
65	2. Implement `main.py`. Use lazy LLM initialization (create clients inside functions, never at module level).
66	
67	3. Generate entry points:
68	
69	   ```bash
70	   uip codedagent init
71	   ```
72	
73	4. Register the agent in the solution — **this is the step that mints the `resource.key`** the flow will reference:
74	
75	   ```bash
76	   cd <SolutionDir>
77	   uip solution project add <CodedAgentProject> <SolutionName>.uipx --output json

83	### Flow Discovery
84	
85	From inside the flow project directory, the agent is discoverable via the in-solution registry. The `--local` flag tells the registry commands to walk up from CWD to find a `.uipx`, read the `resources/solution_folder/process/` files written by step 4, and surface every sibling project as a discoverable node type — all offline, without a tenant registry round-trip:

89	uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json

99	## Wiring the Agent's Inputs
100	
101	For inputs that reference flow variables, use `{ "type": "literal", "expression": "{{ $vars.X }}", "fieldType": "string" }` — NOT `=js:...` expressions. `=js:` ships as a literal string to the agent activity and fails at runtime with `Cannot find name '<identifier>'`.

1	# LangGraph Integration Guide
2	
3	How to build LangGraph agents that work with the UiPath platform. This guide covers project structure, entrypoint detection, LLM models, and common pitfalls.
4	
5	## Scaffolding a New Project
6	
7	If there is **no existing agent code**, scaffold a LangGraph project with:
8	
9	```bash
10	mkdir my-agent && cd my-agent
11	uip codedagent new my-agent
12	```
13	
14	This generates `main.py` (with a StateGraph template), `langgraph.json`, and `pyproject.toml`. Then modify `main.py` to implement your actual agent logic.
15	
16	> **Prerequisite:** `uipath-langchain` must be installed for the LangGraph template to be used. If you get a base template instead, install `uipath-langchain` first.
17	
18	## Project Structure
19	
20	LangGraph agents use a **different structure** from coded function agents. There are two supported patterns:
21	
22	### Pattern A: `langgraph.json` (Recommended for LangGraph)
23	
24	```
25	my-agent/
26	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
27	├── langgraph.json        # Graph configuration — maps names to graph variables
28	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies (must include uipath-langchain)
29	├── .env                  # Environment variables
30	└── ...                   # Generated by uip codedagent init
31	```
32	
33	**`langgraph.json`** tells the runtime where to find your graph:
34	
35	```json
36	{
37	  "graphs": {
38	    "agent": "./main.py:graph"
39	  }
40	}
41	```
42	
43	- `"agent"` — the entrypoint name (used with `uip codedagent run agent`)
44	- `"./main.py:graph"` — path to the Python file and the variable name (`file:variable`)
45	- The file can be named `main.py` or `graph.py` — just ensure the path matches
46	
47	### Pattern B: `uipath.json` with `functions`
48	
49	For agents that use `main.py` instead of `graph.py`:
50	
51	```
52	my-agent/
53	├── main.py               # LangGraph definition — exports `graph` variable
54	├── uipath.json           # UiPath config with functions mapping
55	├── pyproject.toml        # Dependencies
56	└── ...
57	```
58	
59	**`uipath.json`** maps the graph entrypoint:
60	
61	```json
62	{
63	  "$schema": "https://cloud.uipath.com/draft/2024-12/uipath",
64	  "runtimeOptions": {
65	    "isConversational": false
66	  },
67	  "packOptions": {
68	    "includeUvLock": true
69	  },
70	  "functions": {
71	    "graph": "main.py:graph"
72	  }
73	}
74	```
75	
76	### Which Pattern to Use?
77	
78	| Pattern | When to Use |
79	|---------|-------------|
80	| `langgraph.json` | New LangGraph projects, multi-graph setups |
81	| `uipath.json` functions | Existing UiPath projects adding a LangGraph graph |
82	
83	Both patterns require the `graph` variable to be a compiled `StateGraph` or `CompiledStateGraph`.
84

86	
87	## Required Dependencies
88	
89	Every LangGraph agent needs these in `pyproject.toml`:
90	
91	```toml
92	[project]
93	name = "my-agent"
94	version = "0.0.1"
95	description = "My LangGraph agent"
96	requires-python = ">=3.11"
97	dependencies = [
98	    "uipath",
99	    "uipath-langchain",
100	]

102	[dependency-groups]
103	dev = [
104	    "uipath-dev",
105	]
106	```

108	**Key point:** `uipath-langchain` is required — it registers the LangGraph runtime factory that enables `uip codedagent run`, `uip codedagent init`, and deployment to detect and execute your graph.
109	
110	For agents that use LLM calls, add the appropriate model dependency:

122	
123	## LLM Models
124	
125	Use UiPath's LLM libraries instead of raw `langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI`. These route through UiPath's LLM Gateway for centralized model management and billing.
126	
127	### UiPathAzureChatOpenAI (Passthrough)
128	
129	Drop-in replacement for LangChain's `ChatOpenAI` that routes through UiPath's passthrough endpoint (Azure OpenAI API format). No API keys needed — usage consumes Agent Units from your UiPath account.
130	
131	Instantiate LLM clients inside graph nodes or functions — module-level instantiation fails during `uip codedagent init`. See [../lifecycle/build.md](../lifecycle/build.md) § Additional Instructions for the full rule.
132	
133	```python
134	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
135	
136	# Inside a graph node:
137	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(
138	    model="gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18",
139	    temperature=0.7,
140	    max_tokens=4000,
141	    timeout=30,
142	    max_retries=2
143	)
144	```
145	
146	**Model names:** Pass the model identifier as a string. Run `uip codedagent list-models` to list the models available in your tenant.
147	
148	**Features:**
149	- No API key needed — uses UiPath authentication
150	- Supports streaming, structured output, and tool calling
151	- Integrates seamlessly with LangChain agents and RAG
152	
153	### UiPathChat (Normalized)
154	
155	Versatile model class supporting multiple vendors through UiPath's normalized LLM Gateway API. Ideal for multi-vendor strategies.
156	
157	```python
158	from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathChat
159	
160	llm = UiPathChat(
161	    model="gpt-4o-2024-11-20",
162	    temperature=0.5,
163	    max_tokens=2000
164	)
165	```
166	
167	**Supported Models Include:**
168	- **OpenAI**: `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `o3-mini-2025-01-31`
169	- **Anthropic**: `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0`
170	- **Google**: `gemini-2.0-flash-001`
171	- **AWS & Others**: Additional models based on your region and account
172	
173	**Features:**
174	- Supports multiple model providers
175	- Custom streaming headers for compatibility
176	- Flexible model switching for cost/quality optimization
177	- Regional availability may vary by data residency requirements
178	
179	### Configuration Parameters
180	
181	Both models support these configuration options:
182	
183	- `temperature` (0-1): Controls randomness vs. determinism (default: 0.7)
184	- `max_tokens`: Maximum response length (default varies by model)
185	- `timeout`: API request timeout in seconds
186	- `max_retries`: Number of retries on transient failures (default: 2)
187	- `top_p`: Nucleus sampling parameter for diversity
188	- `frequency_penalty`: Reduce token repetition
189	- `presence_penalty`: Encourage new topics
190	
191	### Structured Output
192	
193	Both models support `with_structured_output()` for Pydantic schema validation:
194	
195	```python
196	from pydantic import BaseModel
197	
198	class Analysis(BaseModel):
199	    sentiment: str
200	    confidence: float
201	
202	llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
203	structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(Analysis)
204	raw_dict: dict = await structured_llm.ainvoke("Analyze: I love this product!")
205	result: Analysis = Analysis.model_validate(raw_dict)
206	```
207	
208	### Model Selection Guide
209	
210	| Use Case | Class |
211	|----------|-------|
212	| Cost-conscious, general tasks | `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
213	| Complex reasoning, state-of-the-art | `UiPathChat` or `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI` |
214	| Multi-vendor flexibility (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) | `UiPathChat` |
215	| Specialized domains (e.g., code) | `UiPathChat` with a Claude model |

217	Run `uip codedagent list-models` to see the model strings available in your tenant and pass the exact `model_name` to the class constructor.

220	
221	## Graph Definition
222	
223	### Input/Output Schemas
224	
225	Define `GraphInput` and `GraphOutput` as Pydantic models. These become the agent's schema for `uip codedagent init` and deployment:
226	
227	```python
228	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
229	
230	class GraphInput(BaseModel):
231	    query: str = Field(description="The user's question")
232	    max_results: int = Field(default=5, description="Max results to return")
233	
234	class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
235	    answer: str = Field(description="The answer")
236	    sources: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Sources used")
237	```
238	
239	### State Definition
240	
241	Use `MessagesState` for agents that need conversation history, or a plain `TypedDict`/`BaseModel` for simpler workflows:
242	
243	```python
244	from langgraph.graph import MessagesState
245	
246	class GraphState(MessagesState):
247	    query: str
248	    answer: str | None = None
249	    sources: list[str] | None = None
250	```
251	
252	### Building the Graph
253	
254	```python
255	from langgraph.graph import START, END, StateGraph
256	from langgraph.types import Command
257	
258	async def search(state: GraphState) -> Command:
259	    # ... your logic ...
260	    return Command(update={"answer": "result", "sources": ["url1"]})
261	
262	builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput)
263	builder.add_node("search", search)
264	builder.add_edge(START, "search")
265	builder.add_edge("search", END)
266	
267	graph = builder.compile()
268	```
269	
270	**Important:** The variable MUST be named `graph` and be a `CompiledStateGraph`. This is what the runtime factory looks for.
271	
272	### Runtime Output Quirk — No Channel Reducers For Output Fields
273	
274	The UiPath LangGraph runtime captures the **last node's update delta** as the final output (`runtime.py` uses `stream_mode=["updates",...]` and overwrites `final_chunk` per event). Channel reducers like `Annotated[list, operator.add]` accumulate inside the graph but **do not appear in `--output-file` JSON or eval trajectories** — only the terminal node's delta does.
275	
276	For any aggregate field that must appear in the output, carry it forward explicitly instead of relying on a reducer:
277	
278	```python
279	return {"items": [*state.get("items", []), new_item]}
280	```
281	
282	Or have the terminal node compute the full aggregate and emit it.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## Tracing
287	
288	LangGraph agents get **automatic tracing** — you do NOT need `@traced()` on graph nodes. The UiPath LangGraph runtime instruments all node executions, LLM calls, and tool invocations automatically.
289	
290	Use `@traced()` only on helper functions **outside** the graph that you want to monitor:
291	
292	```python
293	from uipath.tracing import traced
294	
295	@traced(name="postprocess", span_type="tool")
296	async def postprocess(text: str) -> str:
297	    """This gets its own trace span because it's not a graph node."""
298	    return text.strip().lower()
299	```
300	
301	---
302	
303	## Running `uip codedagent init`
304	
305	After creating your graph, generate project configuration:
306	
307	```bash
308	uv sync
309	uip codedagent init
310	```
311	
312	### How Entrypoint Detection Works
313	
314	1. `uip codedagent init` loads all registered middleware via Python entry points
315	2. The `uipath-langchain` package registers a LangGraph middleware
316	3. The middleware checks for `langgraph.json` — if found, it handles init
317	4. If no `langgraph.json`, the standard init checks `uipath.json` `"functions"` field
318	5. The runtime imports your Python file and validates the `graph` variable
319	6. Input/Output schemas are extracted from the graph's `input`/`output` type annotations
320	
321	### Troubleshooting `uip codedagent init`
322	
323	**"No function entrypoints found"**
324	- Ensure `langgraph.json` exists with the correct `"graphs"` mapping, OR
325	- Ensure `uipath.json` has a `"functions"` entry pointing to your graph
326	- The file path and variable name must match exactly (e.g., `"./main.py:graph"`)
327	
328	**Import errors during init / authentication failures**
329	- `uip codedagent init` imports your Python file to introspect the graph
330	- Module-level `UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()` or `UiPathChat()` will try to authenticate on import and fail
331	- **Fix: Move LLM instantiation inside functions/nodes, never at module level:**
332	  ```python
333	  # BAD — fails during uip codedagent init:
334	  llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
335	
336	  # GOOD — lazy initialization inside a node:
337	  async def my_node(state):
338	      llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI()
339	      return await llm.ainvoke(state["messages"])
340	  ```
341	
342	**Schema not detected**
343	- Ensure your `StateGraph` specifies `input_schema=GraphInput, output_schema=GraphOutput` 
344	- The Input/Output classes must be Pydantic `BaseModel` subclasses
345

362	## Conversational Agents
363	
364	For the cross-framework contract (the `isConversational` flag, local-run options), see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md`.
365	
366	### In-Process Input
367	
368	Type the graph state's `messages` field as a list of `AnyMessage` with the `add_messages` reducer:
369	
370	```python
371	from typing import Annotated
372	from langchain_core.messages import AnyMessage
373	from langgraph.graph.message import add_messages
374	from pydantic import BaseModel
375	
376	class State(BaseModel):
377	    messages: Annotated[list[AnyMessage], add_messages] = []
378	```
379	
380	`langgraph.graph.MessagesState` is the equivalent shorthand.
381	
382	The wire envelope (see `../capabilities/conversational-agents.md` § Wire Envelope) lands as the `messages` field; the `uipath-langchain` runtime converts each `UiPathConversationMessage` dict into a LangChain `HumanMessage` before the graph runs.
383	
384	### Two Implementation Options
385	
386	Both are valid — pick based on the agent's needs:
387	
388	- **Prebuilt ReAct agent** — `from langchain.agents import create_agent`. The input contract above is already wired in; just export the compiled graph from your entry point.
389	- **Custom graph** — any `StateGraph` topology consuming the same `messages` field. The first node can be fully deterministic (e.g. validation or routing) before any LLM call.
390

from langgraph.graph import START, StateGraph, END
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class GraphInput(BaseModel):
    sentence: str = Field(description="A sentence describing the outcome of a proposal review round")


class GraphOutput(BaseModel):
    approver_count: int = Field(description="The number of people who approved the proposal")


class GraphState(BaseModel):
    sentence: str = Field(description="A sentence describing the outcome of a proposal review round")
    approver_count: int = Field(default=0, description="The number of people who approved the proposal")


async def analyze_review(state: GraphState) -> GraphState:
    from uipath_langchain.chat.models import UiPathAzureChatOpenAI
    from pydantic import BaseModel as PydanticBaseModel, Field as PydanticField

    class ReviewAnalysis(PydanticBaseModel):
        approver_count: int = PydanticField(
            description="The number of distinct people who explicitly approved the proposal"
        )

    llm = UiPathAzureChatOpenAI(
        model="gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18",
        temperature=0,
        max_tokens=512,
        timeout=30,
        max_retries=2,
    )
    structured_llm = llm.with_structured_output(ReviewAnalysis)

    prompt = (
        "You are analyzing the outcome of a proposal review. "
        "Read the following sentence and identify every person mentioned. "
        "For each person, determine their action: approved, requested changes, or recused. "
        "Count only those who APPROVED. "
        "Return ONLY the integer count of approvers.\n\n"
        f"Review sentence: {state.sentence}"
    )

    raw = await structured_llm.ainvoke(prompt)
    result = ReviewAnalysis.model_validate(raw)
    return GraphState(sentence=state.sentence, approver_count=result.approver_count)


builder = StateGraph(GraphState, input=GraphInput, output=GraphOutput)
builder.add_node("analyze_review", analyze_review)
builder.add_edge(START, "analyze_review")
builder.add_edge("analyze_review", END)

graph = builder.compile()

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. 1	# Wiring Node Outputs to Downstream Inputs
2	
3	How to reference one node's output (or any `$vars.*` value) from another node's input fields. This is the **single source of truth** for `=js:` expression rules in `.flow` JSON. All node-type plugins (connector, http, script, decision, end, etc.) defer to this file.
4	
5	> **Read this before** writing any field that needs to reference a previous node's output, a workflow variable, or any other `$vars.*` / `$metadata.*` value. Skipping `=js:` is the #1 cause of "the value at runtime was the literal string `vars.X.output.Id`" failures (MST-9107).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## The Rule (one sentence)
10	
11	**Any string that references `$vars.*`, `$metadata.*`, or `$self.*` MUST start with `=js:`. Otherwise it is a literal string at runtime.**
12	
13	---
14	
15	## What Goes Wrong Without `=js:`
16	
17	The Flow runtime serializes string fields into BPMN. The serializer rewrites the canvas-form tokens (`$vars` → `vars`) **whether or not the `=js:` prefix is present**. This means a missing prefix is silent — `flow validate` passes, the file looks plausible, but at runtime the BPMN engine sees a plain string and never evaluates it.
18	
19	Three failure modes observed in agent-generated `.flow` files:
20	
21	| What the agent wrote | What ships to runtime | Result |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — invented `nodes.` prefix has no meaning. |
24	| `"$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Literal string — `$vars` rewritten to `vars` but no `=js:` so never evaluated. |
25	| `"=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"=js:vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | Evaluates correctly. |
26	
27	**There is no "nodes.X.output.Y" syntax.** Variable references always use `$vars.*`.
28	
29	---
30	
31	## The Canonical Pattern
32	
33	```
34	"=js:$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output.<field>"
35	```
36	
37	- `<sourceNodeId>` — the `id` value of the node that produces the output
38	- `output` — the literal string `output` (the standard output port; use `error` for errors)
39	- `<field>` — the field path within the output object
40	
41	### Examples
42	
43	| What you want | Expression |
44	|---|---|
45	| The whole output object | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output` |
46	| One field from a single-record output | `=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id` |
47	| A field from the first record of a query result (array) | `=js:$vars.queryEntityRecords1.output[0].Id` |
48	| Filter on a value from a previous node | `=js:$vars.fetchUser1.output.id === $vars.input.userId` |
49	| A static value (no variables) | `"HDFC Bank"` (no prefix needed) |
50	| A built-in metadata value | `=js:$metadata.instanceId` |
51	| A literal that contains a variable | `` =js:`Hello ${$vars.userName}` `` |
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Where the Rule Applies
56	
57	`=js:` is **required** in every field below when the value references `$vars`, `$metadata`, or `$self`:
58	
59	| Node / context | Field | Required `=js:`? |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **Connector activity nodes** (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity>`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
62	| | `inputs.detail.queryParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
63	| | `inputs.detail.pathParameters.*` (all values) | **YES** |
64	| **Managed HTTP** (`core.action.http.v2`) | `inputs.detail.bodyParameters.url` / `headers` / `query` / `body` — both manual and connector mode store dynamic fields here in the `.flow` JSON, regardless of how the CLI's `--detail` flag accepts them at the top level | **YES** |
65	| **Custom HTTP** (`core.action.http`) | `inputs.url` / `headers` / `body` / `queryParams` (deprecated; prefer `core.action.http.v2`) | **YES** |
66	| **HTTP branches** | `inputs.branches[].conditionExpression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
67	| **Decision** (`core.logic.decision`) | `inputs.expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
68	| **Switch** (`core.logic.switch`) | `inputs.cases[].expression` | **NO** — already JS, do not prefix |
69	| **End nodes** (`core.control.end`) | `outputs.<varId>.source` | **YES** |
70	| **Variable updates** | `variables.variableUpdates.<nodeId>[].expression` | **YES** (the CLI auto-prefixes if missing, but write it explicitly) |
71	| **Loop nodes** (`core.logic.loop`) | `inputs.collection` | **YES** |
72	| **Subflow nodes** (`core.subflow`) | `inputs.<inputId>.source` | **YES** |
73	| **Script nodes** (`core.action.script`) | `inputs.script` body — `$vars.*` is read inside JS, no `=js:` wrapping | **NO** — the body is already JS |
74	| **Inline-agent prompt** (`uipath.agent.autonomous` `agent.json` `messages[].content`) | Tokens reference upstream flow nodes directly: `{{ $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] }}` (spaced braces). Mirror in `contentTokens[]` as `{ "type": "variable", "rawString": " $vars.<flowNodeId>.output[.<field>] " }` — `rawString` must include leading and trailing space. Never `{{input.<id>}}` and never bare `{{name}}`. | **NO** — `{{ ... }}` tokens, not `=js:`. See [author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md § Wiring Flow Variables into Agent Prompts](../author/references/plugins/inline-agent/impl.md#wiring-flow-variables-into-agent-prompts). |
75	
76	**Rule of thumb:** If the field is *value-typed* (anything other than a hardcoded condition), `=js:` is required for `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` references. The two condition fields (Decision, Switch) and the script body are the only exceptions — they are always parsed as JS regardless.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Connector Node Wiring — Quick Reference
81	
82	For connector nodes (`uipath.connector.*`), the most common wiring patterns:
83	
84	```jsonc
85	"inputs": {
86	  "detail": {
87	    "method": "POST",
88	    "endpoint": "/v2/{entityName}/UpdateEntityRecord",
89	    "pathParameters": {
90	      "entityName": "BankDetails"
91	    },
92	    "queryParameters": {
93	      "recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id",
94	      "expansionLevel": "3"
95	    },
96	    "bodyParameters": {
97	      "BankName": "HDFC Bank",
98	      "AccountId": "=js:$vars.queryAccounts1.output[0].Id",
99	      "Notes": "=js:`Created from flow run ${$metadata.instanceId}`"
100	    }

task_id: skill-flow-coded-agent
description: >
  Create a UiPath Flow that uses an ApproverCount coded agent to count, from a
  free-text sentence describing each reviewer's stance, how many people approved
  a proposal and return that integer. The sentence is deliberately withheld from
  the prompt and injected by the check script at debug time via --inputs, so the
  agent cannot hardcode the answer or fit a regex to known text — a deterministic
  Function is not a viable design. The prompt explicitly asks for a coded agent
  on a natural-language task, so the resulting flow node must be
  uipath.core.agent (an Agent project), not uipath.core.function — verifying the
  skill honors an explicit agent request instead of substituting a deterministic
  Function. Exercises agent resource node discovery and wiring for coded (vs
  low-code) agents.
tags: [uipath-maestro-flow, e2e, lifecycle:generate, shape:single-node, resource, path-to-ga]

run_limits:
  expected_turns: 35
  turn_timeout: 1200

initial_prompt: |
  Create a UiPath Flow project named "ApproverCountAgent" that uses a coded
  agent named "ApproverCount" to analyze a sentence describing the outcome of
  a proposal review round. The flow takes the sentence as a string input
  variable. The agent must identify each person mentioned, determine whether
  they approved, requested changes, or recused themselves, and return the
  number of people who approved as an integer flow output.

  Validate the flow.
  Do NOT ask for approval, confirmation, or feedback. Do NOT pause between planning and implementation. Build the complete flow end-to-end in a single pass.

success_criteria:
  # ── Flow file validity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - type: run_command
    description: "uip maestro flow validate passes on the flow file"
    command: "uip maestro flow validate ApproverCountAgent/ApproverCountAgent/ApproverCountAgent.flow"
    timeout: 30
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 3.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  # ── Execution checks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - type: run_command
    description: "Flow has an agent node and debug returns the approver count"
    command: "python3 $TASK_DIR/check_coded_agent_flow.py"
    timeout: 360
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 5.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

post_run:
  - command: "python3 $SKILLS_REPO_PATH/tests/tasks/uipath-maestro-flow/_shared/cleanup_solutions.py"
    timeout: 120

agent.system_prompt.value: You are a coding agent. Do not access files in sibling runs/* directories. Everywhere else is permitted.

parameters.description: Scaffold the coded agent

parameters.command: cd /work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-coded-agent/ApproverCountAgent && uip maestro flow init "ApproverCountAgent" --output json 2>&1
parameters.description: Scaffold flow project inside solution

parameters.command:
\
source .venv/bin/activate && \
cd ApproverCount && \
uip codedagent init 2>&1
parameters.description: Run codedagent init to generate entry-points and schemas

parameters.command:
cd /work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-coded-agent/ApproverCountAgent && \
uip solution project add "ApproverCount" "ApproverCountAgent.uipx" --output json 2>&1
parameters.description: Register coded agent in solution to mint resource.key

parameters.command:
cd /work/output/artifacts/skill-flow-coded-agent/ApproverCountAgent/ApproverCountAgent && \
uip maestro flow registry list --local --output json 2>&1
parameters.description: List local flow registry to find the agent node type
